title: Detention and Tryouts
premise: Lena Okonkwo, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, has survived three years by being perfectly, invisibly fine—until detention forces her into a semester-long project with Theo Marchetti, the headmaster's son and her longtime nemesis. Digging into the academy's archives for their project, they uncover that the school's generous 'scholarship fund' is a front for quietly expelling students who ask too many questions, and that Lena's own enrollment was sponsored by someone with an agenda. As their reluctant partnership deepens into trust and then love, they must decide whether to expose the truth knowing it will cost Lena her scholarship, Theo his father, and both of them the fragile belonging they've finally found. In the end, they testify before the board together: the academy is reformed, Lena loses her scholarship but gains a community that refuses to let her go, and she learns that survival bought with silence was never really living.
about_author: Elodie Eriksen is a former boarding school teacher who spent six years watching brilliant students learn to hide in plain sight. She writes stories about the kids who were told to be grateful and decided to be loud instead.

chapters.title: Perfectly Fine
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A tour through Lena's carefully managed life at Ashgrove: flawless grades, invisible presence, and a mental list of rules for surviving on scholarship. When she nearly misses breakfast because she stayed up covering a shift, we see the cost of 'fine.' Emotional beat: exhaustion disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Owns the Hallways
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Establishing the nemesis dynamic: Theo Marchetti, headmaster's son, gets away with everything while Lena gets scrutinized for everything. A collision in the corridor ends with both of them blamed equally—and only one of them punished. Emotional beat: the injustice that fuels her.

chapters.title: Saturday Detention
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Both land in Saturday detention after the corridor incident; Ms. Adeyemi sentences them to co-author a semester project on the academy's history. They negotiate hostile truce terms like diplomats. Emotional beat: grudging recognition that the enemy is smarter than expected.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo narrates his side—the weight of being the headmaster's son, his father's expectations, and why he needles Lena specifically. He proposes dividing the archive work to avoid each other. Emotional beat: loneliness hiding inside privilege.

chapters.title: Dust and Dead Names
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. First archive session in the basement stacks. Lena finds a 1998 student newspaper mentioning a 'withdrawal' that doesn't match any record. Theo dismisses it; Lena can't let it go. Emotional beat: the itch of a question that won't close.

chapters.title: The Scholarship List
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo pulls the old scholarship ledgers to prove Lena wrong and instead finds gaps—years where funded students simply vanish from enrollment mid-term. He says nothing to his father. Emotional beat: first crack in loyalty to family.

chapters.title: Truce Over Cold Pizza
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Working late, they share contraband pizza and compare notes; the hostility thaws into something like respect. Lena admits how much the scholarship means—her whole family's pride rests on it. Emotional beat: vulnerability exchanged like currency.

chapters.title: Withdrawn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They track down Priya Nair, a vanished scholarship student, now working two towns over. Priya warns them: 'Ashgrove doesn't expel you. It makes you want to leave.' She refuses to say more. Emotional beat: fear arriving ahead of evidence.

chapters.title: Midterms and Misdirection
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The headmaster notices Theo spending time in the archives and assigns him a prestigious fellowship designed to occupy him. Lena feels the project—and the alliance—slipping. Emotional beat: jealousy she refuses to name.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers his father personally signed off on Priya's 'voluntary withdrawal.' He lies to his father's face for the first time. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of seeing a parent clearly.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Late night in the stacks, a near-kiss interrupted by a security guard; both retreat into banter. Lena realizes staying invisible is no longer possible—with the school or with him. Emotional beat: terror and thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: The Sponsor File
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They find Lena's own file: her scholarship was created the year she applied, funded by an anonymous donor connected to a foundation the headmaster chairs. Her admission wasn't luck—it was design. Emotional beat: the ground giving way beneath identity.

chapters.title: Why Me?
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena spirals—was she chosen as a token, a shield, or bait? She pushes Theo away, accusing him of running his father's errands even here. Emotional beat: self-protection weaponized against the person who matters most.

chapters.title: Ms. Adeyemi's Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their faculty advisor reveals she was a vanished student too—she stayed silent to keep her job, and she begs them to do the math on what exposure costs. Emotional beat: a cautionary mirror of their possible futures.

chapters.title: The Fellowship Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a donors' dinner, Theo hears his father toast the scholarship program as 'an investment in the right kind of student.' Theo publicly stumbles, drawing his father's cold fury. Emotional beat: open rupture between father and son.

chapters.title: Choosing Sides Out Loud
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Theo comes to Lena's dorm with the full ledger trail and apologizes—not for his father, but for ever making her feel like a project. They reconcile and commit to going public together. Emotional beat: love declared as alliance, not escape.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The administration moves first: Lena is placed on 'academic review,' a prelude to quiet removal, and the archive access is revoked. They have days, not months. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: Everything We Stole Back
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A heist-flavored chapter: with help from Priya, Ms. Adeyemi, and dorm allies, they copy the ledgers and record testimony from three more vanished students. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself out of shared damage.

chapters.title: Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Climax part one: they present the evidence to the trustees. Theo accuses his father publicly, choosing truth over blood. The headmaster counters by revealing Lena's sponsor file, framing her as compromised. Emotional beat: courage priced in real time.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax part two: Lena speaks last, refusing to be a victim or a token—she names every vanished student and claims her place at Ashgrove on merit, not charity. The board votes to suspend the headmaster pending investigation. Emotional beat: voice as victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fallout: Theo's father resigns; Theo loses his name's currency and gains his own. Lena's scholarship is dissolved with the corrupt program—but students, faculty, and alumni crowdfund a new one with her name on its charter. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude tangled together.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Epilogue in spring: the new scholarship's first applicants arrive, and Lena—no longer invisible—gives the welcome speech. Theo waits for her afterward, hand outstretched. She takes it. Emotional beat: survival rewritten as belonging.
